title: Pros and Cons of Microservices
description: Evaluate scalability, complexity, operational overhead, and data consistency trade-offs.

data.text: Microservices offer compelling benefits like independent scaling and team autonomy, but they also introduce significant complexity. Understanding both sides is essential before committing to the architecture.

terms.definition: The ability to handle increased load by adding resources.
The cost of running, monitoring, and maintaining distributed systems.
The guarantee that data remains correct across multiple services.
The ability to contain failures to a single service.

items: Independent scaling: Scale only the services that need it
Technology diversity: Choose the best tool for each service
Team autonomy: Teams own services end to end
Fault isolation: Failures do not cascade across the system
Network complexity: Services communicate over the network
Data consistency: Distributed transactions are hard
Operational overhead: More services to deploy and monitor
Testing complexity: End-to-end testing is harder
Debugging complexity: Tracing requests across services

data.text: Each microservice requires its own deployment pipeline, monitoring, logging, and alerting. A system with 50 services needs 50 CI/CD pipelines, 50 monitoring dashboards, and 50 alert configurations. This overhead is manageable with platform engineering but significant for small teams.

In a monolith, a single database transaction ensures consistency. In microservices, each service owns its data, so cross-service transactions require distributed patterns like Saga, Two-Phase Commit, or eventual consistency.

data.caption: Microservices Scalability vs Monolith
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Monolith[🏢 Monolith Scaling]
        A[App] --> B[Scale Entire App]
        B --> C[All Components Scale Together]
    end
    subgraph Micro[🔗 Microservices Scaling]
        D[Service A] --> E[Scale A Only]
        F[Service B] --> G[Scale B Only]
        H[Service C] --> I[Scale C Only]
    end

data.title: Exercise: Cost-Benefit Analysis
data.description: For a hypothetical application with 5 services, calculate the operational overhead versus the scalability benefits.
steps: List the 5 services and their expected load patterns
Estimate the infrastructure cost for monolith vs microservices
Calculate the team overhead for each approach
data.expectedOutcome: A written analysis with cost estimates and a justified recommendation

items.question: When do microservices not pay off?
items.answer: When the team is small, the domain is simple, or the scale does not justify the operational overhead.

items.question: What is the hidden cost of microservices?
items.answer: Operational overhead: deployment, monitoring, and debugging distributed systems.

items.question: How do you measure microservices success?
items.answer: Track deployment frequency, mean time to recovery, and service ownership clarity.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Microservices offer independent scaling and team autonomy
They introduce network complexity and operational overhead
The decision depends on team size, domain complexity, and scale
data.takeaway: Microservices are a trade-off: more scalability and autonomy for more complexity and overhead.
